title: How Sweet, How Calm, This Sabbath Morn
description: How Sweet, How Calm, This Sabbath Morn in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 374, “Sabbath Morning”, where the book credits them to Christian Hymns.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How sweet, how calm, this Sab-bath morn! How pure the air that breathes! How soft the sounds up-on it borne! How light its va-por wreathes!

lines: How sweet, how calm, this Sabbath morn!
How pure the air that breathes!
How soft the sounds upon it borne!
It seems as if the Christian's prayer,
For peace and joy and love,
Were answered by the very air
And every care that mars our peace
In Faith and Love be hushed.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
